properties.statement: EVERY TOOL RESULT THIS SERVER HAS EVER SENT CARRIED ITS PAYLOAD TWICE, BYTE FOR BYTE — once as `structuredContent` and once as a text `content` block. The reasoning was sound (`json_result`: 'so clients reading either both get the data') and the cost was never measured. It is a flat 2× on every reply, and it is why three separate rollups are refused by harnesses rather than one: `detect_gaps` at 79,566 chars of payload = 157,785 bytes on the wire, `graph_report` at 88,932 and 91,330, `loop_status` at 72,886. || THE FIX IS ONE LINE AND THE CHOICE INSIDE IT IS THE INTERESTING PART. An EMPTY `content` block saves exactly the same bytes. A SIGNPOST — one sentence naming the field the payload is in — costs ~450 bytes against payloads in the tens of thousands, and is what a client reading the wrong field gets INSTEAD OF SILENCE. Silence there is indistinguishable from reflow2 never having been configured, which is `req:never-silently-absent` and the reason `proxy.rs` keeps a process on stdio whatever state the server is in. So the cheaper option was rejected for the one that fails loudly. || WHY NOT THE OBVIOUS ANSWER, and this is the measurement that killed it: gate the duplication on the negotiated protocol version. `structuredContent` arrived in MCP `2025-06-18` and rmcp 3.1.2 still negotiates `2024-11-05` and `2025-03-26`, so a client that predates the field is genuinely reachable — the version is not a hypothetical. BUT the negotiated version lives on the `RequestContext`, and OF 156 TOOL HANDLERS EXACTLY ONE TAKES ONE (`claim_region`, for the seat). Gating meant threading a context through the other 155 and all 151 `ok_json` call sites, to protect a client nobody could name, against a signpost that protects them for one line. ⇒ THE CHEAP CORRECT FIX AND THE PRINCIPLED-LOOKING ONE WERE 1 LINE AND ~300 LINES, AND THE PRINCIPLED-LOOKING ONE WAS PROPOSED FIRST, BEFORE ANYONE COUNTED. || ANTHONY'S OWN CLIENTS WERE NEVER AT RISK AND THIS WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: all three in-repo Python clients (smoke_mcp, reflow2_cli, reflow2_check) read `structuredContent` FIRST and fall back to `content` only when it is absent; the `j!` macro every Rust tool test uses reads `structured_content` only; `proxy.rs` forwards raw JSON-RPC bytes and parses neither field; and prose tools (`ok_markdown`) never wrote `structuredContent` at all, so `content` remains their only carrier and is untouched. || MEASURED EFFECT, this design, 77 open gaps: 157,785 bytes on the wire before any of this work, 53,181 after the reply budget, 26,096 after the signpost — 6×, with the payload itself unchanged at 27,846 characters. || SOURCE: measured 2026-08-23 on reflow2 0.38.0, driving the built binary over real stdio. Decided by Anthony the same day after being shown the options.
